blind_spots.blind_spot: The spatial-registration accuracy that carries the proposal was measured in open space, on a topic that is specifically about enclosed and constrained-access inspection
blind_spots.operator_reality: Motion-capture reference balls and environment recognition need line of sight; inside a wing box, a fuel cell, or behind a bulkhead, half the markers are occluded and the AR overlay drifts off the part. The maintainer then does what maintainers always do — pulls the headset off and goes back to the paper tech order — and the evaluation records the capability as not ready. The fix is architectural and cheap if made now: degrade gracefully to a marker-on-part local frame with a stated accuracy floor for confined space, and publish that number instead of the open-space one.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The open-space figures are genuinely impressive and already in hand, so they get reused as the proposal's proof rather than treated as the wrong test condition for this topic.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Better than 0.5 mm x, y, z accuracy has already been achieved in open spaces

blind_spots.blind_spot: The entire capability rides on third-party AR headsets whose product lifecycles are shorter than a Navy sustainment cycle
blind_spots.operator_reality: A V-22 wiring-harness inspection program lives for a decade; the headsets it was authored against get discontinued in two or three. When the display vendor exits, every authored procedure is stranded, the government owns content it cannot run, and the re-host is unfunded. On the flight line there is also nobody assigned to charge, sanitize, ESD-protect, or account for the devices, and no spares line — which is how a successful pilot quietly dies between the demo and the second squadron. Naming a hardware-abstraction layer and a device-refresh plan in the transition package is what keeps the content asset alive.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their own abstract flags a hardware trade study as a Phase II objective, which frames device choice as an optimization problem rather than as a decade-long obsolescence and sustainment risk the government has to fund.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The hardware upgrades will be a "trade study"-like objective for Phase II. With the increasing availability and deployment of new hardware supporting computer vision and AR, Team AVATAR needs to ensure that SIA QA works on the equipment and hardware most likely to be employed by maintenance crews.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Every named champion is an engineer or unit-level user; no program office or PEO sponsor appears anywhere
blind_spots.operator_reality: A branch engineer at NSWC Port Hueneme and an EOD company commander can get a capability tried; neither can put it on a POM line, and without POM money the work resets to the next SBIR topic every eighteen months. That is the mechanism behind twenty-three years, twenty-nine people, and repeated Phase IIs with no program of record — enthusiasm at the operator level substituting for an acquisition sponsor. Identifying the specific PMA or PEO that owns V-22 maintenance training, and getting a transition agreement signed while the Phase II is still funded, is the single highest-leverage move available.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The testimonials are genuinely warm and they read like traction, so the missing layer above them is easy not to notice until the funding stops.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "This project proves AVATAR's ability to provide XR training with different equipment and increases opportunities at the USCG." Ron Stark, Human Performance Technology Manager | Force Readiness Command, Training Division

opener_hook: The Air Force topic AVATAR won in 2022 is nondestructive evaluation in enclosed or constrained-access locations, and the proposal's tracking numbers — 0.5 mm position, 3 degrees orientation — are both qualified as achieved in open spaces, which is the gap that usually shows up at the first confined-space demo rather than in the lab.
what_they_do: Builds AI-assisted augmented and virtual reality maintenance and training software (XRcreate authoring platform) for Navy and Air Force maintainers, inspectors, and EOD teams, plus commercial aerospace and healthcare customers.
